heroHeadline: Three Days to Sindoor Anniversary: Bilawal Hails Pakistan's 'Marka-e-Haq Triumph' as Rajnath Inaugurates Shaurya Symposium
heroSubtitle: On May 4, 2026 — three days before the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor (May 7, 2025) — Pakistan and India launched competing anniversary mobilizations. Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari addressed a Sindh government event in Karachi marking 'Marka-e-Haq' (Pakistan's name for the May 2025 confrontation), declaring Pakistan 'not a nation that bows' and calling the outcome a 'triumph of resolve, unity, and dignity' — Pakistan's formal counter-narrative to India's voluntary-halt and nuclear-bluff framing. Simultaneously, Rajnath Singh inaugurated the three-day Shaurya Defence Technology Symposium in New Delhi, declaring that 'Operation Sindoor showed India's military capabilities to the world.' The dueling commemorations crystallize the competing narratives ahead of the May 7 anniversary: India asserting strategic dominance and deterrence reestablishment; Pakistan asserting defensive resilience and diplomatic success. The bilateral standoff remains unchanged: airspace closed until May 24 (both sides), Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all trade halted, IWT at UNSC. India's 4th S-400 regiment is en route from Russia and arriving mid-May. India's military spending is now 5th globally at $92.1B (SIPRI 2025), while Pakistan's Delimitation Bill controversy (24 AJK seats reserved) adds a constitutional dimension to the anniversary-week tensions. The Shaurya Symposium continues through May 6, with the core anniversary (May 7) and ceasefire anniversary (May 10) still ahead.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
